output.summary: KEP-5471 extends core/v1 Toleration with numeric comparison operators Lt and Gt so pods can match node taints such as node.kubernetes.io/sla=950 by threshold. The KEP is at status implementable, stage alpha, behind a feature gate, and its scope is limited to the TaintToleration plugin.
output.rationale: Platform teams want to keep most workloads off lower-SLA (spot/preemptible) nodes while letting specific workloads opt in with thresholds like SLA ≥ 95%. Existing Equal and Exists tolerations cannot express "any value above a threshold" without enumerating every value. The design keeps the taint/toleration safety model, including NoExecute eviction, and reuses operators already known from NodeAffinity.

alternatives.why_not: Creates new API surface and breaks the unified taint/toleration model, per the Alternatives section.
Requires maintaining an out-of-tree plugin and does not use the existing taint/toleration infrastructure.

alternatives.option: Separate NumValue int64 field on Taint/Toleration
alternatives.why_not: Dual fields are unaesthetic and error-prone; reviewers agreed reusing Value is better and the field can be added later if needed.

alternatives.option: Use Equal with numeric values only
alternatives.why_not: Pods must enumerate exact values and cannot express ranges like SLA > 950 or accept any low-SLA node.

evidence.quote: Extend **core/v1 Toleration** to support **numeric comparison operators** when matching **Node Taints**: - New operators: `Lt`, `Gt`
Primary motivation: allow pods to opt‑in to nodes by `SLA/failure‑probability` values published as taints
Is it fair to add a goal to ensure that the addition of new operators has zero operational effect on existing pod scheduling outcomes
As we agreed on [this](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/5473#discussion_r2269966442) feedback, we removed the `Ge` and `Le` operators.

The [current validation](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go#L4326-L4339) is strict and it explicity rejects any operator that isn't `Equal` or `Exists`.
